title: Burn-rate forecasting and automated throttling policy for model variants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: We currently rely on static circuit breakers and manual error-budget interventions to protect latency and availability SLOs for model endpoints. As traffic patterns diversify across tenants and routes, these reactive measures either trigger too late (causing SLO violations) or are overly conservative (causing unnecessary capacity loss).

Goal: Implement a per-endpoint and per-model-variant burn-rate forecasting system that predicts short-term error-budget burn and automatically triggers graded throttling actions (soft throttles, variant fallback, batching tweaks) to keep SLOs within target without manual intervention. The system should be safe-by-default, auditable, and integrate with existing circuit-breaker and failover orchestration.

Scope:
- Forecast error-budget burn for each model variant at 1m, 5m, and 15m horizons.
- Define actionable thresholds (soft, medium, hard) that map to automated throttling policies.
- Implement a decision engine that emits enforcement decisions and a separate enforcement layer that applies throttles via existing rate-limiters and routing knobs.
- Provide dashboards, alerting, and an incident runbook.
- Ensure manual overrides and tenant-aware exceptions.

Out of scope for this ticket: wholesale rework of circuit-breaker framework, billing changes, and on-prem only network enforcement (will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Forecasting pipeline produces per-variant burn-rate predictions for 1m/5m/15m horizons and stores results in metrics DB with <= 10s latency from ingestion
Decision engine evaluates thresholds and emits throttle decisions within 3s of crossing a threshold
Enforcement layer applies soft throttles (reduce max tokens / increase sampling) and variant fallback within 5s and logs actions to activity stream
End-to-end tests demonstrate recovery from synthetic surge without exceeding configured per-endpoint SLOs in 9/10 trials
Operator dashboard shows predicted burn vs observed burn, runway estimate, recent enforcement actions, and link to runbook
Playbook and postmortem template published in Confluence with checklist for manual rollback and customer communication
implementation_steps: Instrument additional metrics: per-variant requests_total, successful_tokens, error_tokens, latency_histogram, and token_cost_estimate
Build a lightweight forecasting microservice using EWMA + short-window ARIMA fallback (python) with pluggable feature flags
Expose predictions as prometheus-style metrics: burn_forecast_1m, burn_forecast_5m, burn_forecast_15m with labels (endpoint, model, variant, region)
Create decision engine (go) that subscribes to forecasts and current error_budget_balance and emits decisions to enforcement topic (kafka) with decision_reason and ttl
Enhance rate-limiter and routing layer to accept enforcement messages: actions = [soft_throttle, reduce_max_tokens, prefer_cheap_variant, disable_prefetch, increase_batch_window]
Add audit logging: who/what/why/timestamp for every enforcement action and backfill to data warehouse for analysis
Wire dashboards (Grafana) for predicted vs observed burn, runway minutes, and per-tenant risk heatmap
Create e2e test harness that can inject synthetic surges and validate decision + enforcement latency and correctness
Run staged rollout: staging -> canary (10% traffic across two clusters) -> 50% -> 100% with kill-switch and manual approval gates
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): deploy forecasting service + decision engine, smoke tests against historical traces
Phase 1 (canary): enable enforcement for non-critical routes only; log decisions but do not apply enforcement; validate false-positive rate
Phase 2 (limited-enforcement): enable soft throttles for low-risk tenants and routes, monitor customer impact for 48h
Phase 3 (aggressive-enforcement): add cheaper-variant fallback and medium throttles for burst-prone endpoints; maintain manual override for 72h
Phase 4 (global): enable across all hosted clusters after 2 weeks of stable metrics and runbook approvals
monitoring_queries: SQL (analytics): SELECT variant, region, avg(predicted_burn_5m) as predicted, avg(observed_burn_5m) as observed FROM burn_forecasts WHERE ts > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY variant, region
Alert rule: if predicted_runway_minutes < 10 for any customer_tier = 'production' for two consecutive checks -> P1 alert to oncall
runbook: If P1 alert fires (predicted_runway_minutes < 10): 1) Check decision stream for recent enforcement actions and reasons, 2) If enforcement is active, toggle enforcement to 'log-only' (kill-switch) for affected endpoint, 3) If traffic surge continues, open an incident and coordinate with capacity team to provision burst nodes

If false-positive throttles observed: 1) Identify offending rule in decision engine, 2) Add temporary exception for tenant (tenant-exception tag) and create follow-up to refine model, 3) Re-run e2e tests against replayed trace
When rolling back: ensure audit log contains timestamped enforcement messages and post-rollback join with telemetry to verify SLOs are stable
Communication: notify account managers for any customers impacted by enforced throttling and copy incident channel with timeframe and mitigation steps

2026-02-28 - Emma Rodriguez (SRE): Reviewed enforcement plan. Requested safety gates: (1) enforcement TTL of 2 minutes, (2) per-tenant opt-out label, (3) audit logs stored for min 90 days.
2026-03-04 - Product (Noah Singh): Requested explicit UX on Console for 'throttle history' with per-tenant view. Added to acceptance criteria.
